items.heading: Headache
details: Rest in a quiet, dimly lit room and drink a glass of water.
Apply a cold compress to the forehead or a warm compress to the back of the neck, whichever feels better.
Gently massage the temples, or apply a small amount of peppermint or clove oil.
A cup of ginger or chamomile tea can help with a mild tension headache.
See a doctor if the headache is sudden and severe, recurring frequently, or comes with vision changes, confusion, or fever.

items.heading: Stomach ache or mild indigestion
details: Sip warm water, or warm ajwain (carom seed) water, slowly.
Chew a small piece of ginger, or drink ginger tea, to ease discomfort.
Avoid heavy, oily, or spicy food until it settles.
A hot water bag on the abdomen can relieve cramping.
See a doctor if the pain is severe, persists beyond a day, or comes with fever or vomiting.

items.heading: Acidity or heartburn
details: Drink cold milk, or chew a few tulsi (basil) leaves, for quick relief.
Avoid lying down immediately after eating - stay upright for at least 30 minutes.
Avoid spicy, oily, and caffeinated food until it settles.
See a doctor if it happens frequently, or is accompanied by chest pain.

items.heading: Common cold and cough
details: Drink warm fluids like ginger tea, turmeric milk (haldi doodh), or warm water with honey and lemon.
Gargle with warm salt water to soothe a scratchy throat.
Try steam inhalation to help clear nasal congestion.
Rest well and stay hydrated.
See a doctor if fever is high, symptoms last beyond 7-10 days, or breathing becomes difficult.

items.heading: Sore throat
details: Gargle with warm salt water several times a day.
Sip warm turmeric milk or a honey-ginger tea.
Suck on a piece of clove or a lozenge to soothe irritation.
See a doctor if it is severe, lasts more than a week, or comes with high fever or difficulty swallowing.

items.heading: Nausea or vomiting
details: Sip small amounts of water or an ORS solution frequently, rather than large gulps.
Try ginger tea, or a small piece of raw ginger with a pinch of salt.
Rest and avoid solid food until the stomach settles, then reintroduce bland food gradually.
Seek medical help if vomiting is persistent, contains blood, or comes with severe abdominal pain.

items.heading: Mild diarrhea
details: Drink an ORS (oral rehydration solution) or a homemade salt-sugar water solution frequently to prevent dehydration.
Eat bland foods like rice, banana, and curd once able to eat again.
Avoid dairy other than curd, caffeine, and oily food temporarily.
See a doctor promptly if there is blood in the stool, high fever, or signs of dehydration such as dizziness or very little urination.

items.heading: Constipation
details: Drink plenty of water throughout the day.
Eat fibre-rich foods like fruits, vegetables, and whole grains.
A warm glass of milk with a teaspoon of ghee at bedtime can help.
Light physical activity or a short walk can stimulate digestion.
See a doctor if it persists beyond a week or is accompanied by pain or bleeding.

items.heading: Toothache
details: Rinse the mouth with warm salt water.
Apply a cold compress to the cheek near the painful tooth to numb discomfort.
A clove, or a drop of clove oil, on the affected tooth can numb the pain temporarily.
See a dentist as soon as possible - a toothache usually signals an underlying issue that needs treatment.

items.heading: Hiccups
details: Hold your breath for about 10 seconds, then swallow, and repeat a few times.
Sip cold water slowly, or swallow a teaspoon of sugar.
Breathe into a paper bag for a short time - never a plastic bag.
See a doctor if hiccups persist for more than 48 hours.

items.heading: Muscle cramp
details: Gently stretch and massage the cramped muscle.
Apply a warm compress, or take a warm shower, to relax the muscle.
Stay hydrated and replenish electrolytes, especially after exercise or heat exposure.

items.heading: Mild fever
details: Rest and drink plenty of fluids like water, coconut water, and warm soups.
Use a lukewarm sponge bath or a cool compress on the forehead to bring the temperature down.
Wear light, breathable clothing rather than bundling up.
See a doctor if fever exceeds 39.4 C (103 F), lasts more than 3 days, or comes with a rash, stiff neck, or difficulty breathing.
